name: LTR-329 ambient light sensor
description: Lite-On digital ambient light sensor with two 16-bit channels (visible+infrared and infrared), gains 1x-96x and 50-400 ms integration, covering about 0.01 to 64k lux, I2C at fixed address 0x29; the chip runs on 2.4-3.6 V. Sold as: Adafruit LTR-329 Light Sensor - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (#5591), 5-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA with a 3.3 V regulator and I2C level shifting for 3-5 V.
eli5: Tells your board how bright the light around it is, from a dark room to full sunlight.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3-5 V (on-board regulator makes 3.3 V for the chip)

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 k pull-up and level shifter on board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 k pull-up and level shifter on board)

supplierQuery: LTR-329 ambient light sensor breakout I2C
buildNotes: Wait at least 100 ms after power-up, then write ALS_CONTR (0x80) = (gain << 2) | 1 to leave standby; the first result is ready 10 ms wake-up plus one integration later.
ALS_MEAS_RATE (0x85) = (integration code << 3) | repeat-rate code; the default 0x03 is 100 ms integration every 500 ms. Integration time must not exceed the repeat rate.
Read the data as one 4-byte block from 0x88: CH1 (infrared) low, high, then CH0 (visible + infrared) low, high. Reading CH1 first is required: the registers stay locked until 0x8B is read.
ALS_STATUS (0x8C) bit 2 = new data, bit 7 = data invalid (discard and wait).

Lux (Lite-On Appendix A): ratio = CH1/(CH0+CH1); below 0.45: 1.7743*CH0 + 1.1059*CH1; below 0.64: 4.2785*CH0 - 1.9548*CH1; below 0.85: 0.5926*CH0 + 0.1185*CH1; else 0. Divide by gain and by integration time in units of 100 ms.
A channel at 65535 is saturated: lower the gain (1x covers up to about 64k lux). Use 48x or 96x only for dim indoor light.
The address 0x29 is fixed: one LTR-329 per I2C bus (the TSL2591 and VL53L0X also use 0x29).

driver.code:
# LTR-329 ambient light sensor (Lite-On LTR-329ALS-01, datasheet DS86-2014-0006), MicroPython driver.
# I2C address 0x29 (fixed), 8-bit registers. Two 16-bit ADC channels, LSB first:
#   CH1 (infrared) at 0x88/0x89, CH0 (visible + infrared) at 0x8A/0x8B.
# The datasheet says to read 0x88..0x8B in order (CH1 first): the four data registers are locked
# until 0x8B has been read, so both channels come from the same measurement. We read all four in one go.
# Lux uses the Lite-On "Appendix A" formula (ratio = CH1 / (CH0 + CH1)), divided by gain and
# integration time in units of 100 ms.
import time

_ALS_CONTR = 0x80
_ALS_MEAS_RATE = 0x85
_PART_ID = 0x86
_MANUFAC_ID = 0x87
_ALS_DATA_CH1_0 = 0x88
_ALS_STATUS = 0x8C

# ALS gain codes (ALS_CONTR bits 4:2); 4 and 5 are reserved
GAIN_1X = 0
GAIN_2X = 1
GAIN_4X = 2
GAIN_8X = 3
GAIN_48X = 6
GAIN_96X = 7
_GAIN_X = {0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 4, 3: 8, 6: 48, 7: 96}

# Integration time codes (ALS_MEAS_RATE bits 5:3) -> milliseconds
INT_100MS = 0
INT_50MS = 1
INT_200MS = 2
INT_400MS = 3
INT_150MS = 4
INT_250MS = 5
INT_300MS = 6
INT_350MS = 7
_INT_MS = (100, 50, 200, 400, 150, 250, 300, 350)

# Measurement repeat rate codes (ALS_MEAS_RATE bits 2:0) -> milliseconds
RATE_50MS = 0
RATE_100MS = 1
RATE_200MS = 2
RATE_500MS = 3
RATE_1000MS = 4
RATE_2000MS = 5
_RATE_MS = (50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000)


class LTR329:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x29, gain=GAIN_1X, integration=INT_100MS, rate=RATE_500MS):
        if gain not in _GAIN_X or integration not in range(8) or rate not in range(6):
            raise ValueError('use the GAIN_, INT_ and RATE_ constants')
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.gain = gain
        self.integration = integration
        self.rate = rate
        time.sleep_ms(100)  # initial start-up time after power is applied (datasheet: 100 ms)
        if self._r8(_PART_ID) >> 4 != 0xA or self._r8(_MANUFAC_ID) != 0x05:
            raise OSError('LTR-329 not found at 0x%02X (check the wiring)' % addr)
        # Integration time must not exceed the repeat rate, or the chip clamps it to the rate.
        self._w8(_ALS_MEAS_RATE, (integration << 3) | rate)
        self._w8(_ALS_CONTR, (gain << 2) | 0x01)  # gain + active mode
        time.sleep_ms(10)  # wake-up time from standby (max 10 ms)
        self._wait_ms = 10 + max(_INT_MS[integration], _RATE_MS[rate])

    def _r8(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    def _w8(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val]))

    def channels(self):
        """Wait for a fresh, valid measurement and return (ch0, ch1) counts:
        ch0 = visible + infrared, ch1 = infrared only."""
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while True:
            st = self._r8(_ALS_STATUS)
            if st & 0x04 and not st & 0x80:  # bit 2: new data, bit 7: data invalid
                break
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) > 2 * self._wait_ms + 500:
                raise OSError('LTR-329: no new data (check the wiring)')
            time.sleep_ms(10)
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _ALS_DATA_CH1_0, 4)  # 0x88, 0x89, 0x8A, 0x8B in order
        ch1 = d[0] | (d[1] << 8)
        ch0 = d[2] | (d[3] << 8)
        return ch0, ch1

    def lux(self, ch0=None, ch1=None):
        """Illuminance in lux (Lite-On Appendix A). Returns 0 in the dark or for IR-dominated light,
        None if a channel is saturated (65535: lower the gain or integration time)."""
        if ch0 is None:
            ch0, ch1 = self.channels()
        if ch0 >= 65535 or ch1 >= 65535:
            return None
        if ch0 + ch1 == 0:
            return 0.0
        ratio = ch1 / (ch0 + ch1)
        if ratio < 0.45:
            lux = 1.7743 * ch0 + 1.1059 * ch1
        elif ratio < 0.64:
            lux = 4.2785 * ch0 - 1.9548 * ch1
        elif ratio < 0.85:
            lux = 0.5926 * ch0 + 0.1185 * ch1
        else:
            return 0.0
        return lux / _GAIN_X[self.gain] / (_INT_MS[self.integration] / 100)

    def standby(self):
        """Stop measuring (about 5 uA)."""
        self._w8(_ALS_CONTR, self.gain << 2)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ltr329 import LTR329, GAIN_1X, INT_100MS, RATE_500MS

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = LTR329(i2c, gain=GAIN_1X, integration=INT_100MS, rate=RATE_500MS)
while True:
    ch0, ch1 = sensor.channels()
    print('CH0=%d CH1=%d Lux=%.1f' % (ch0, ch1, sensor.lux(ch0, ch1)))
    time.sleep(1)
